meta.title: Kant's one rule for knowing right from wrong

plates.query: Vincent van Gogh Starry Night over the Rhône painting
plates.want: Van Gogh, the starry heavens above (PD)

plates.query: Caspar David Friedrich Two Men Contemplating the Moon

beats.text: Kant wanted a test for right and wrong that needed no god, no reward, no exception.
He found one rule. Before you act, look at the reason behind the act.
Then ask: could I will that everyone, always, acted on this same reason?
Lying fails instantly. If everyone lied when it suited them, no promise could mean anything.
So never treat a person as a mere tool, he said. Treat them always as an end in themselves.
Two things filled him with awe: the starry heavens above him, and the moral law within.
Morality isn't a feeling to Kant. It's a law you could hand to all of humanity without shame.

attribution: Immanuel Kant · Critique of Practical Reason
source_note: Quote: Critique of Practical Reason, trans. T. K. Abbott (public domain).
